recipes.title: Choose a graphical sequence-analysis and cloning workbench
recipes.description: Match the workbench to the laboratory task: broad sequence analysis, supported project workflows, or visual cloning design.

picks.label: Open graphical analysis workspace
picks.reason: Combines sequence viewing, annotation, alignment tools and visual workflows.
picks.tradeoff: External tools and reference databases add dependencies; validate each selected method.

picks.label: Supported integrated laboratory workflow
picks.reason: Brings mapping, alignment, cloning, automation and project management into a commercial desktop environment.
picks.tradeoff: Subscriptions, cloud entitlements and academic eligibility differ by plan.

picks.label: Visual cloning design and documentation
picks.reason: Plasmid maps, cloning simulation and edit history make construct design inspectable.
picks.tradeoff: Free Viewer mode supports inspection and annotation; full cloning design requires a paid subscription.

recipes.title: Create and inspect biological sequence alignments
recipes.description: Distinguish alignment computation from manual inspection. Difficult regions and biological assumptions still need review before tree inference.

picks.label: Scriptable alignment generation
picks.reason: Offers several sequence-alignment strategies and workflows for adding sequences to an existing alignment.
picks.tradeoff: Strategy choice and package licenses vary; inspect ambiguous alignment regions.

picks.label: Alignment interpretation with annotations
picks.reason: Links alignment editing and analysis with biological annotations and molecular structure views.
picks.tradeoff: Some services require a network connection, and external analyses have their own assumptions.

picks.label: Focused alignment inspection
picks.reason: Provides a dedicated viewer/editor with navigation suited to checking alignment columns and sequence labels.
picks.tradeoff: External aligners and Java packaging require separate setup.

recipes.title: Choose a phylogenetic inference method and interface
recipes.description: Choose by statistical question and workflow, then check models, support and uncertainty. These tools do not establish one universally best tree.

picks.label: Model-aware maximum likelihood
picks.reason: Combines maximum-likelihood inference, model selection, branch support and checkpointing.
picks.tradeoff: Alignment quality and model assumptions remain critical; complex models can consume substantial resources.

picks.label: Explicit scripted likelihood searches
picks.reason: Provides tree-search, parameter-optimization and bootstrap controls for reproducible analyses.
picks.tradeoff: Windows uses WSL; search replicates and settings must be justified.

picks.label: Graphical molecular-evolution analysis
picks.reason: Presents evolutionary distances and tree methods in an integrated graphical environment.
picks.tradeoff: Its no-charge terms are limited to research and education, with redistribution restrictions.

picks.label: Bayesian dated-tree models
picks.reason: Samples trees and parameters to represent posterior uncertainty in time-aware evolutionary models.
picks.tradeoff: Check priors, convergence, effective sample sizes and independent chains before interpretation.

picks.label: Display a legacy tree project
picks.reason: Provides branch/node display and annotation controls for tree figures.
picks.tradeoff: FigTree is superseded by PearTree; neither viewer replaces inference or convergence diagnostics.

recipes.title: Inspect reads, genome annotations and assembly graphs
recipes.description: Pick the data representation first: mapped reads, curated annotations, complex genome views or assembly-graph connectivity.

picks.label: Locus-level read and track review
picks.reason: Displays aligned-read and genomic-track evidence in a local desktop session.
picks.tradeoff: Large datasets need valid indexes and compatible reference coordinates.

picks.label: Extensible complex genome views
picks.reason: Supports a pluggable desktop workspace with multiple genomic representations.
picks.tradeoff: Plugins and input formats need preparation; the separate web deployment is a different product route.

picks.label: Genome annotation curation
picks.reason: Combines sequence-feature inspection with editing and comparative tools.
picks.tradeoff: Java and optional database workflows add setup requirements.

picks.label: Focused assembly and alignment viewing
picks.reason: Concentrates on visual review of sequencing assemblies and mapped reads.
picks.tradeoff: A visible pattern still needs an appropriate analytical method before drawing conclusions.

picks.label: Assembly-graph connectivity
picks.reason: Shows connections and branches that disappear in a flat contig file.
picks.tradeoff: Current packages differ by platform, and graph topology alone does not prove assembly correctness.

recipes.title: Inspect, preprocess and summarize sequencing quality
recipes.description: These tools cover complementary stages: diagnose raw reads, apply justified preprocessing, then compare results across samples.

picks.label: Per-file diagnostic reports
picks.reason: Reports sequencing quality and composition patterns before or after preprocessing.
picks.tradeoff: Warning thresholds are heuristics and can reflect legitimate assay properties.

picks.label: Preprocessing with recorded reports
picks.reason: Combines quality filtering, adapter trimming and HTML/JSON reporting in a scripted step.
picks.tradeoff: Trimming can remove useful sequence; tune settings for the actual library.

picks.label: Cross-sample report aggregation
picks.reason: Collects supported tool outputs into a project-level overview.
picks.tradeoff: It does not perform the underlying measurements; module recognition and sample naming affect aggregation.

recipes.title: Select a command-line tool for a genomic file operation
recipes.description: Choose by data model instead of treating every sequence utility as interchangeable.

picks.label: FASTA and FASTQ sequences
picks.reason: Filters, transforms, extracts and summarizes sequence records with self-contained executables.
picks.tradeoff: Check identifiers, strand handling and coordinate conventions.

picks.label: SAM, BAM and CRAM alignments
picks.reason: Sorts, indexes, filters and converts mapped-read alignment files.
picks.tradeoff: Reference and sorting assumptions must match downstream tools; Windows setup differs.

picks.label: Genomic interval relationships
picks.reason: Intersects, merges and compares regions such as genes, peaks and coverage intervals.
picks.tradeoff: BED and GFF coordinate conventions differ; current source and older docs also carry different license labels.

picks.label: Mapping long reads or assemblies
picks.reason: Aligns sequence data to a reference using task-specific presets.
picks.tradeoff: It is a mapper rather than a general file editor; this record verifies the published Linux binary route.

recipes.title: Choose a BIM authoring environment
recipes.description: Start with team deliverables, native operating-system needs, exchange formats and the authoring model.

picks.label: Revit-centered multidisciplinary delivery
picks.reason: Connects architectural, structural and building-services models with documentation.
picks.tradeoff: Native Windows requirement and separately licensed collaboration services can affect the toolchain.

picks.label: Architectural BIM on Windows or Mac
picks.reason: Combines architectural modeling, documentation and team workflows with native desktop options.
picks.tradeoff: Plan entitlements and consultant exchange requirements need agreement before a project starts.

picks.label: DWG-based transition into BIM
picks.reason: Places building-modeling and IFC tools alongside familiar DWG drafting workflows.
picks.tradeoff: Some integrations vary by OS; perpetual and subscription entitlements differ.

picks.label: Open IFC authoring inside Blender
picks.reason: Creates native IFC data with linked drawings, schedules and Python automation.
picks.tradeoff: It requires compatible Blender and is labeled alpha; test exchange and workflow stability on representative projects.

recipes.title: Review IFC deliverables and city-scale semantic models
recipes.description: A dedicated viewer suits reviewers who do not need a full authoring license. Check format coverage and paid extensions before selecting one.

picks.label: Focused IFC stakeholder review
picks.reason: Provides building geometry and property inspection with a free core viewer.
picks.tradeoff: Optional plugins have separate licenses and the installer flow requests an email address.

picks.label: IFC, gbXML and CityGML review
picks.reason: Connects building-scale and city-scale semantic formats with property and relationship inspection.
picks.tradeoff: Requires Windows runtime components; open plugin code does not imply an open-source application license.

picks.label: Review that may become IFC authoring
picks.reason: Native IFC editing can help when inspection uncovers data that must be changed.
picks.tradeoff: A Blender extension and alpha authoring workflow bring more setup than a standalone viewer.

recipes.title: Plan interior layouts and architectural concepts
recipes.description: Match the tool to the level of design detail: rooms and furniture, flexible spatial concepts or data-rich building models.

picks.label: Rooms and furniture
picks.reason: Links a floor plan with three-dimensional furniture placement and interior views.
picks.tradeoff: Free and paid distributions bundle different assets; it is not a full building-engineering system.

picks.label: Flexible spatial concept modeling
picks.reason: Supports direct 3D modeling with extensions and plan-dependent documentation tools.
picks.tradeoff: Desktop subscriptions, web access and Studio features have different capabilities and terms.

picks.label: Concepts that need native IFC data
picks.reason: Connects geometry with building classifications, properties and coordinated documentation.
picks.tradeoff: Requires Blender and familiarity with IFC/BIM workflows; current Studio is alpha.

recipes.title: Choose a building-energy modeling workflow
recipes.description: Separate the simulation engine from graphical model preparation and from legacy project compatibility.

picks.label: Detailed simulation engine
picks.reason: Provides whole-building thermal and HVAC simulation for scripted or interface-driven workflows.
picks.tradeoff: Requires carefully prepared geometry, schedules, weather and system assumptions.

picks.label: Open graphical EnergyPlus workflow
picks.reason: Adds graphical model editing and compatible simulation components around the OpenStudio ecosystem.
picks.tradeoff: Application, SDK and SketchUp plugin are separate products; verify release compatibility.

picks.label: Commercial integrated performance analysis
picks.reason: Combines model preparation with licensed energy, daylight, HVAC and other analysis modules.
picks.tradeoff: Required modules affect cost; results still depend on validated model assumptions.

picks.label: Existing DOE-2 project compatibility
picks.reason: Supports established eQUEST models, wizards and energy-efficiency comparisons.
picks.tradeoff: The public download is older and current maintenance is unverified; confirm project and compliance requirements.

recipes.title: Choose a lighting and luminaire planning tool
recipes.description: Both tools offer a free core, but manufacturer participation and paid extensions change practical project coverage.

picks.label: Luminaire-based lighting design
picks.reason: Covers indoor, outdoor, street and emergency lighting calculations and documentation.
picks.tradeoff: Non-member luminaires and some export/productivity features require paid plans.

picks.label: Lighting with sensor planning
picks.reason: Combines artificial-light/daylight calculations with luminaire and sensor planning.
picks.tradeoff: Non-member product presentation and specialist extensions have separate licensing; native Windows is required.

recipes.title: Choose a desktop life-cycle assessment workflow
recipes.description: Software choice does not supply the inventory data or settle model assumptions. Compare database access, scripting needs and model transparency.

picks.label: Graphical multi-database LCA work
picks.reason: Provides process networks, impact assessment and exchange with several LCA data ecosystems.
picks.tradeoff: Commercial background databases and services may cost extra despite the free application.

picks.label: Brightway-connected analysis
picks.reason: Brings graphical project and inventory editing to the Python/Brightway ecosystem.
picks.tradeoff: Environment compatibility and separately licensed datasets require setup and review.

recipes.title: Choose CAD/CAM software for a CNC project
recipes.description: Match the design source, required machining strategies, machine output and edition restrictions before generating a job.

picks.label: Compact 2D and 3D preparation
picks.reason: Generates toolpaths from drawings, meshes and images with an optional compatible control workflow.
picks.tradeoff: Free mode adds file-operation delays; paid version 13 updates have a one-year entitlement period.

picks.label: Integrated design for Carbide machines
picks.reason: Combines vector drawing, simulation and 2D/2.5D machining in Core.
picks.tradeoff: Standard G-code for other machines and advanced 3D work require Pro.

picks.label: Decorative routing and signs
picks.reason: Provides V-carving, decorative toolpaths and machining of imported relief models.
picks.tradeoff: It is a paid Windows product; the trial cannot cut arbitrary user-created designs.

picks.label: Imported geometry to machining
picks.reason: Offers a permanent free entry point and paid advanced/multi-axis editions.
picks.tradeoff: Edition capabilities and the selected postprocessor must match the machine.

picks.label: Blender-centered CAM
picks.reason: Keeps geometry and toolpath work in the Fabex CNC Blender extension.
picks.tradeoff: Requires compatible Blender/dependencies and careful postprocessor validation.

picks.label: Multiple fabrication processes
picks.reason: Provides browser, desktop and local-server routes for milling, laser and printing preparation.
picks.tradeoff: Machine profiles and deployment-specific storage behavior need verification.

recipes.title: Arrange vector parts on sheet material
recipes.description: Nesting tools propose layouts; verify paths, units, spacing and the downstream cutting process before using the result.

picks.label: Browser-based SVG nesting
picks.reason: Packs irregular SVG parts with spacing, rotation and part-in-part controls.
picks.tradeoff: Input geometry must be prepared as suitable paths, and heuristic nesting does not guarantee a global optimum.

picks.label: Desktop nesting and shared cuts
picks.reason: Adds a desktop workflow with common-line merging and DXF conversion.
picks.tradeoff: Confirm any external conversion path; the released MIT desktop repository differs from the separate rewrite.

recipes.title: Choose software for preparing and sending laser jobs
recipes.description: Start with the controller, then decide whether integrated drawing, engraving preparation or a free focused sender is the priority.

picks.label: Integrated multi-controller workflow
picks.reason: Combines layout, editing, job settings and supported controller communication.
picks.tradeoff: Core/Pro compatibility depends on controller type; current Linux support is limited to legacy releases.

picks.label: Free GRBL-focused Windows workflow
picks.reason: Prepares raster engraving jobs and sends them to compatible GRBL controllers.
picks.tradeoff: It is not a universal laser driver; verify the actual machine and material settings.

picks.label: Fabrication preparation in a browser
picks.reason: Can prepare laser jobs alongside milling and 3D-printing workflows.
picks.tradeoff: Generated jobs still require a compatible machine profile and sending/control route.

recipes.title: Measure a room, loudspeaker or live audio signal
recipes.description: Choose the measurement method before the interface. Calibrated microphones, sound-card routing and repeatable measurement conditions matter more than a polished plot.

picks.label: Room and loudspeaker response
picks.reason: Combines acoustic measurements, response views and equalizer-filter planning.
picks.tradeoff: Correct microphone calibration, timing and placement are required; an equalizer cannot repair every room problem.

picks.label: Live transfer-function workflow
picks.reason: Provides real-time spectrum, transfer-function and sound-level views.
picks.tradeoff: Sound-level accuracy depends on calibration and hardware; confirm platform pricing and distribution.

picks.label: Immediate signal inspection
picks.reason: Provides spectrum, spectrogram and scope views for an incoming audio signal.
picks.tradeoff: An attractive spectrum is not a calibrated room-acoustics report.

recipes.title: Reduce noise in an existing recording
recipes.description: These are conditional choices for recorded files or editor sessions. Compare the noise type, available edition and listening result on a copy of your source.

picks.label: Detailed restoration modules
picks.reason: Provides dedicated spectral and voice restoration workflows with noise-only monitoring.
picks.tradeoff: Module and standalone-editor availability vary by edition; strong processing can remove wanted speech.

picks.label: Editing with restoration in one workspace
picks.reason: Combines waveform/spectral editing with edition-specific restoration tools.
picks.tradeoff: Standard in-app tools differ from Premium/Ultimate plugins; Linux is currently a public beta.

picks.label: Restoration inside an Adobe audio session
picks.reason: Documents noise-print reduction, adaptive effects and spectral selection.
picks.tradeoff: Subscription licensing applies; offline Noise Reduction is specific to the Waveform Editor.

recipes.title: Choose a desktop audio-processing route
recipes.description: Match input versus playback processing, operating system and routing. Equalization, convolution and speech noise suppression solve different signal problems.

picks.label: Linux microphone and playback effects
picks.reason: Applies configured effects to PipeWire applications and can process microphone audio before the destination app.
picks.tradeoff: Install the selected noise plugin/model, keep hardware defaults as upstream instructs, and verify the destination receives processed input.

picks.label: Windows endpoint equalization
picks.reason: Provides configurable Windows audio processing for supported device paths.
picks.tradeoff: Driver and audio-mode compatibility determine whether processing applies; this record does not establish general-purpose noise suppression.

picks.label: Configured convolution and DSP pipeline
picks.reason: Offers explicit audio-processing pipelines for deliberate routing and filtering setups.
picks.tradeoff: Device backends and configuration require technical setup; measure the complete signal path.

recipes.title: Extract and inspect features from recorded audio
recipes.description: Use reproducible feature extraction when the question needs structured outputs, then review the visual or aligned result before interpreting it.

picks.label: Batch feature extraction
picks.reason: Runs supported audio-analysis plugins and writes machine-readable results.
picks.tradeoff: The selected plugin defines the measurement and may need separate installation or licensing.

picks.label: Detailed visual inspection
picks.reason: Displays and annotates recorded audio with layered analysis views.
picks.tradeoff: Plugin availability and parameter choices affect results; visual patterns need interpretation.

picks.label: Compare aligned recordings
picks.reason: Supports comparison of multiple audio recordings through an aligned visual workflow.
picks.tradeoff: Alignment is an analytical aid and can need correction; it does not prove musical or perceptual equivalence.

recipes.title: Inspect a monophonic vocal melody or speech contour
recipes.description: A singing-note transcription and a phonetic pitch analysis use different assumptions. Check octave errors and unvoiced regions against the recording.

picks.label: Correct an estimated melody transcription
picks.reason: Focuses on pitch and note extraction from monophonic recordings with manual correction.
picks.tradeoff: Polyphonic mixtures and ambiguous note boundaries require more work; automatic output is not ground truth.

picks.label: Speech-oriented acoustic analysis
picks.reason: Provides pitch, spectral and phonetic analysis with scripting.
picks.tradeoff: Pitch range, voicing assumptions and analysis windows must match the speaker and question.

picks.label: Layered listening and inspection
picks.reason: Lets analysts combine waveform, spectrogram and available analysis layers.
picks.tradeoff: Automatic feature extraction may require a suitable Vamp plugin.

recipes.title: Choose a photogrammetry reconstruction workflow
recipes.description: Select the intended output: camera poses, a textured object mesh, or a georeferenced aerial product. Capture overlap, scale control and validation remain essential.

picks.label: Camera reconstruction and sparse/dense stages
picks.reason: Provides graphical and command-line structure-from-motion workflows.
picks.tradeoff: Dense processing has hardware and dependency requirements; reconstructed scale needs external control.

picks.label: Dense mesh after camera registration
picks.reason: Consumes registered images and camera poses to produce dense geometry and textures.
picks.tradeoff: It needs an upstream registration stage and compatible interchange data.

picks.label: Aerial mapping through a web interface
picks.reason: The current WebODM distribution uses ODX for aerial imagery processing and offers official free installers.
picks.tradeoff: The current project is independent of OpenDroneMap; verify the actual engine and deployment route in older tutorials.

picks.label: Commercial integrated reconstruction
picks.reason: Combines reconstruction, inspection and project workflow in a commercial desktop product.
picks.tradeoff: Geospatial and advanced features depend on edition; check hardware and license requirements.

picks.label: Commercial desktop reconstruction route
picks.reason: Offers a photogrammetry pipeline for turning photographs into 3D assets.
picks.tradeoff: Revenue-based eligibility and entitlement terms need checking before assuming no-charge use.

recipes.title: Control a tethered camera from the computer
recipes.description: Check the exact camera model and requested control before selecting an application; USB detection alone does not prove live view or remote exposure support.

picks.label: Windows tethered still photography
picks.reason: Provides remote camera control and supported capture workflows on Windows.
picks.tradeoff: Individual camera models expose different capabilities.

picks.label: Linux tethering through supported cameras
picks.reason: Provides a graphical tethered photography workflow built around camera-control support.
picks.tradeoff: The underlying camera library and device support determine available actions.

picks.label: Frame-by-frame animation capture
picks.reason: Coordinates camera capture with animation review, exposure sheets and optional hardware.
picks.tradeoff: It is a paid production tool; supported camera and motion-control hardware must be checked.

recipes.title: Capture and assemble a stop-motion shot
recipes.description: Choose by the capture equipment and the production controls you need, then test one short shot with the real camera.

picks.label: Coordinated production set
picks.reason: Connects frame capture with exposure, dialogue, lighting and motion-control workflows.
picks.tradeoff: Hardware support and paid entitlements determine the usable feature set; the public FAQ currently links an older EULA.

picks.label: Open animation workspace with capture features
picks.reason: Combines 2D animation tools with supported stop-motion capture workflows.
picks.tradeoff: Camera integration and capture controls differ from a dedicated motion-control setup.

recipes.title: Prepare voice and mouth timing for animation
recipes.description: These tools address separate parts of dialogue production: generating a singing voice, timing phonemes and using those timings in an animation scene.

picks.label: Map recorded dialogue to mouth cues
picks.reason: Provides a focused phoneme and timing workflow for lip synchronization.
picks.tradeoff: Automatic or initial timing needs manual review and a matching mouth-shape set.

picks.label: Use dialogue timing in a 2D scene
picks.reason: Provides an animation environment for assembling character and scene work.
picks.tradeoff: Confirm supported timing interchange and drawing setup; import is not a finished performance.

picks.label: Synthesize a singing performance
picks.reason: Creates singing output from note and lyric data with supported voicebanks.
picks.tradeoff: Voicebank and renderer compatibility and licenses are separate; singing synthesis is not general dialogue lip-sync.

recipes.title: Choose support for a specific desktop access need
recipes.description: Select the access task first: pointer control, reading the interface, magnification or speech input. Verify the application combination with the person using it.

picks.label: Head movement for pointer control
picks.reason: Uses a camera-based head-tracking workflow to move the pointer.
picks.tradeoff: Camera placement, lighting and comfortable movement range affect usability.

picks.label: Windows screen reading
picks.reason: Provides spoken and braille access to supported Windows applications.
picks.tradeoff: Commercial licensing and application-specific accessibility support need checking.

picks.label: Windows magnification and reading support
picks.reason: Combines screen magnification with supported reading features.
picks.tradeoff: Edition and compatibility determine the available reading controls.

picks.label: Local speech/text workflows on Linux
picks.reason: Provides configurable speech recognition and synthesis routes through local models.
picks.tradeoff: Model downloads, hardware support and output quality vary; test the intended language and input device.

recipes.title: Read documents aloud and create personal speech audio
recipes.description: Choose the operating system, text workflow and voice first. The application license and the voice/output license are separate decisions.

picks.label: Windows reading with installed voices
picks.reason: Reads documents and clipboard text with supported Windows voices and can export audio.
picks.tradeoff: Noncommercial use is free; commercial organizations or paid audio distribution require the application license plus appropriate voice rights.

picks.label: Paid Windows reading workflow
picks.reason: Adds word highlighting, selected-text tools and batch audio creation.
picks.tradeoff: Optional Acapela voices are limited to NextUp products and personal generated-audio use unless separate rights are obtained.

picks.label: Configurable local Linux models
picks.reason: Combines text-to-speech with other local speech workflows.
picks.tradeoff: Model licensing, language support and hardware requirements differ from the application itself.

recipes.title: Choose an interface and solver route for CFD
recipes.description: Start from the physical model, mesh and verification plan. A friendlier interface does not validate turbulence, boundary conditions or convergence.

picks.label: Configurable open-source simulation toolkit
picks.reason: The Foundation distribution provides extensible finite-volume CFD workflows.
picks.tradeoff: Solver setup, meshing and scripting require expertise; other OpenFOAM distributions are separate products.

picks.label: Aerodynamic analysis and design research
picks.reason: Provides open-source simulation and adjoint-oriented design methods.
picks.tradeoff: Build features vary; documented prebuilt packages omit discrete-adjoint support.

picks.label: Graphical setup with commercial support options
picks.reason: Presents CFD preparation and analysis through a desktop interface with Windows, Linux and Apple Silicon Mac routes.
picks.tradeoff: The free edition is limited to 200,000 mesh cells and one CPU; paid terms and solver assumptions still matter.

recipes.title: Match a finite-element solver to the engineering problem
recipes.description: Compare the material models, coupling and preprocessing workflow required by the project. Benchmark a known case before interpreting a new model.

picks.label: Scriptable structural and thermal cases
picks.reason: Provides linear/nonlinear, static/dynamic and thermal analysis with an Abaqus-style input approach.
picks.tradeoff: A familiar input style does not guarantee complete Abaqus compatibility; geometry and solver checks remain necessary.

picks.label: Broad structural mechanics workflow
picks.reason: Combines structural analysis with the SALOME/AsterStudy ecosystem and scripted execution.
picks.tradeoff: Linux/container and third-party Windows packages have different installation and support boundaries.

picks.label: Multiphysics coupling
picks.reason: Offers a finite-element suite spanning multiple physical equations.
picks.tradeoff: Each coupled model needs suitable numerical settings and independent validation.

picks.label: Biomechanical constitutive models
picks.reason: Focuses on nonlinear mechanics and multiphysics used in biomechanics.
picks.tradeoff: Specialized material assumptions must match the specimen and loading; solver availability does not validate a biological conclusion.

recipes.title: Start or migrate an airfoil and wing analysis project
recipes.description: Potential-flow tools suit preliminary exploration under their model assumptions. Use more complete CFD only when its additional complexity is justified and validated.

picks.label: Current XFLR5-family starting point
picks.reason: Provides the successor workflow and recent releases for preliminary aerodynamic analysis.
picks.tradeoff: Version 7.58 ends Intel Mac binary packaging and the developer announces no future Linux packages; source builds and old binaries need a plan.

picks.label: Reproduce a legacy analysis
picks.reason: Preserves established airfoil and wing-analysis workflows and project compatibility.
picks.tradeoff: Development closed on 30 June 2026, so new projects should evaluate the successor.

picks.label: Broader CFD research route
picks.reason: Provides a solver and design framework for cases beyond the potential-flow workflow.
picks.tradeoff: It requires a suitable mesh, physical models and verification; it is not a drop-in file replacement.

recipes.title: Choose a water model for the actual hydraulic domain
recipes.description: A pressurized drinking-water network, sewer catchment, river floodplain and groundwater system require different governing models and inputs.

picks.label: Pressurized distribution network
picks.reason: Models hydraulic and water-quality behavior in drinking-water pipe networks.
picks.tradeoff: The Windows GUI and toolkit serve a specific network domain; input demands and calibration control the result.

picks.label: Stormwater and sewer catchments
picks.reason: Models rainfall-runoff, drainage networks and selected green-infrastructure controls.
picks.tradeoff: The official desktop GUI is Windows; a portable computational engine does not imply a matching native GUI.

picks.label: River and floodplain hydraulics
picks.reason: Provides river hydraulic analysis with official Windows desktop tools.
picks.tradeoff: Linux downloads are computational engines, not the Windows graphical application; the HEC software license is not open source.

picks.label: Groundwater flow and transport system
picks.reason: Provides the USGS modular numerical groundwater framework.
picks.tradeoff: Input preparation and conceptual-model design need separate tools and hydrogeological expertise.

recipes.title: Choose a molecular simulation engine
recipes.description: Select by force field, particle model, algorithms and required packages. An installed engine does not establish that the chosen model is scientifically appropriate.

picks.label: Molecular dynamics workflows
picks.reason: Provides a molecular-dynamics engine with documented build and acceleration options.
picks.tradeoff: Force-field preparation, sampling and validation dominate the scientific result; accelerator support depends on the build.

picks.label: Configurable particle interactions
picks.reason: Supports molecular and materials simulation through selectable interaction styles and packages.
picks.tradeoff: A prebuilt executable may omit a required package; record the exact build and configuration.

recipes.title: Inspect simulation particles, trajectories or molecular structures
recipes.description: Choose by data representation and analysis method, then keep visualization settings separate from measured quantities.

picks.label: Particle and atomistic analysis pipelines
picks.reason: Provides visualization and analysis workflows for particle-based simulation data.
picks.tradeoff: Basic and Pro capabilities differ; inspect the license and method requirements for the intended analysis.

picks.label: Molecular trajectory inspection
picks.reason: Provides molecular graphics and trajectory-oriented analysis for supported datasets.
picks.tradeoff: VMD has a custom source-available license, not an OSI open-source license; production and test builds differ by platform.

picks.label: Structures and experimental maps
picks.reason: Combines atomic models with density maps and related molecular data.
picks.tradeoff: Commercial-use conditions differ from free noncommercial use; trajectories and file formats need checking.

recipes.title: Choose a terrain-analysis working style
recipes.description: Begin with the DEM, coordinate system, resolution and drainage assumptions. Interface choice is secondary to preprocessing and interpretation.

picks.label: Graphical geoscientific toolbox
picks.reason: Offers dedicated terrain and raster-analysis modules.
picks.tradeoff: Processing choices and grid resolution can materially change derived landforms or drainage.

picks.label: Scripted local geospatial processing
picks.reason: Exposes terrain, hydrology and LiDAR tools through Python and R.
picks.tradeoff: Next Gen APIs and Python/R binary platforms differ; optional Pro workflows are separately licensed.

picks.label: Integrated raster/vector analysis system
picks.reason: Combines geospatial processing with reusable command-based workflows.
picks.tradeoff: Its data model and environment setup take time to learn.

picks.label: Map-centered desktop workbench
picks.reason: Combines data inspection, editing and access to processing providers.
picks.tradeoff: External provider availability and plugin versions determine which algorithms are actually installed.

recipes.title: Choose a network-analysis environment
recipes.description: A network picture and a biological interaction analysis require different supporting data. Check identifiers, directedness, weights and missing edges before comparing metrics.

picks.label: Interactive exploratory graph figures
picks.reason: Offers network layouts, filters, statistics and visual exports.
picks.tradeoff: The current roadmap still lists complete undo/redo as unfinished; save versions and avoid treating layout distance as scientific evidence.

picks.label: Attributed biological or research networks
picks.reason: Combines network visualization with data integration and an app ecosystem.
picks.tradeoff: App versions, identifiers and external services add dependencies and may have separate terms.

recipes.title: Clean a table or build a visual analysis pipeline
recipes.description: Choose an interactive cleanup tool for inconsistent values, or a workflow system when the analysis needs several repeatable processing stages.

picks.label: Inspect and normalize messy values
picks.reason: Facets, clustering and replayable transformations make table cleanup inspectable.
picks.tradeoff: Reconciliation can send selected data to external services; proposed merges need review.

picks.label: Reusable visual data pipelines
picks.reason: Connects preparation, modeling and optional code through a workflow graph.
picks.tradeoff: Desktop access is free, while Hub deployment/collaboration and some integrations have separate terms.

picks.label: Interactive exploratory analysis
picks.reason: Uses connected widgets for visual data analysis and machine learning.
picks.tradeoff: Widget choices and validation design determine whether model results are meaningful.

recipes.title: Choose an econometric and statistical workflow
recipes.description: Decide which model, diagnostics and reproducibility path you need before choosing the interface. None of these applications makes observational data causal by itself.

picks.label: Econometrics with GUI and scripts
picks.reason: Combines regression, time-series and panel methods with Hansl scripting.
picks.tradeoff: Statistical assumptions and model diagnostics remain the analyst’s responsibility.

picks.label: Programmable statistical environment
picks.reason: Offers broad statistical and graphical packages for scripted analyses.
picks.tradeoff: Package versions, methods and licenses need to be recorded separately.

picks.label: Syntax and graphical statistical workflow
picks.reason: Provides common data-analysis procedures through GUI and command syntax.
picks.tradeoff: Check procedure coverage and interchange compatibility for the specific study.

picks.label: Graphical frequentist/Bayesian analysis
picks.reason: Offers a graphical interface for documented statistical methods.
picks.tradeoff: Available analyses and prior settings must match the research question.

recipes.title: Choose a curve-fitting and plotting tool
recipes.description: Choose by model form, constraints, uncertainty and reporting needs. Residuals and parameter identifiability matter more than a smooth fitted line.

picks.label: Focused overlapping-peak fitting
picks.reason: Provides a dedicated interface for fitting peaks and experimental curves.
picks.tradeoff: Model choice and parameter constraints require domain judgment.

picks.label: Commercial integrated laboratory analysis
picks.reason: Combines fitting, statistics, graph formatting and reusable templates.
picks.tradeoff: Current native releases are Windows-only and advanced functions depend on edition and license.

picks.label: Open scientific plotting workspace
picks.reason: Combines imported data, plotting and fitting in a worksheet-oriented environment.
picks.tradeoff: Confirm the available fit model and interoperability with the lab’s data formats.

picks.label: Table-and-graph analysis workflow
picks.reason: Presents numerical data and scientific plots in a compact graphical workspace.
picks.tradeoff: Check required advanced procedures and current platform packages before standardizing on it.

recipes.title: Select astronomical camera capture software
recipes.description: Capture the night sky with software matched to the camera, driver, platform and observing workflow. High-frame-rate planetary video, live stacking and unattended deep-sky sequencing are distinct tasks.

picks.label: Private planetary acquisition
picks.reason: Focuses on supported astronomical cameras and planetary capture controls.
picks.tradeoff: The license prohibits commercial use, and camera support varies by operating system.

picks.label: Multi-platform supported-camera capture
picks.reason: Provides acquisition packages for Windows, Mac and Linux processor combinations.
picks.tradeoff: ChromeOS support ended; verify the precise camera SDK and architecture.

picks.label: Windows live stacking and EAA
picks.reason: Combines camera acquisition with live image accumulation and optional alignment tools.
picks.tradeoff: Selected functions require annual Pro licensing; unlicensed real-camera Pro testing disables saving.

picks.label: Deep-sky equipment and sequence coordination
picks.reason: Organizes supported equipment, targets, framing and imaging sequences on Windows.
picks.tradeoff: It serves a different acquisition pattern from planetary video; hardware and plugin compatibility must be checked.

recipes.title: Process astronomy captures for an image or measurement
recipes.description: Select visual image production or quantitative photometry first, and preserve the calibration data and processing history needed to assess the result.

picks.label: Calibration, registration and stacking
picks.reason: Provides an astrophotography processing workflow for prepared image sequences.
picks.tradeoff: Calibration frames, rejection settings and color handling influence the output.

picks.label: Astronomical image measurement
picks.reason: Provides calibration and photometry-oriented analysis derived from ImageJ.
picks.tradeoff: Quantitative measurements need appropriate apertures, reference stars and uncertainty checks.

picks.label: Plate solving and FITS inspection
picks.reason: Combines astrometric solving with stacking and related astronomy utilities.
picks.tradeoff: Required star databases and data preparation are separate installation concerns.

recipes.title: Choose a host for audio instruments and effects
recipes.description: Match plugin format, operating system, routing and stage-management requirements. Test the complete audio chain at the intended buffer size.

picks.label: Open plugin hosting and patching
picks.reason: Provides a dedicated host for loading and connecting instruments and effects.
picks.tradeoff: Plugin formats and optional bridges vary by build and operating system.

picks.label: Modular routing graph
picks.reason: Provides configurable audio/MIDI plugin graphs with free public builds.
picks.tradeoff: The no-charge channel trails paid update channels; hosted plugins need their own compatible licenses and binaries.

picks.label: Windows live performance management
picks.reason: Offers free basic VST hosting and paid set-list, routing and state tools.
picks.tradeoff: Advanced performance functions depend on edition; current releases require 64-bit Windows.

recipes.title: Convert an audio collection or extract CDs
recipes.description: Decide whether the target is archival lossless audio, portable listening copies or scripted conversion. Preserve source files when applying DSP or lossy encoding.

picks.label: Open desktop conversion and CD extraction
picks.reason: Combines audio conversion and disc extraction with supported encoders.
picks.tradeoff: Encoder and metadata options require deliberate setup for an archival workflow.

picks.label: Mac cue-sheet and lossless workflow
picks.reason: Provides lossless conversion, cue splitting and CD extraction with GUI and command-line routes.
picks.tradeoff: Mac only; the full source/package license set remains unresolved in this review.

picks.label: Commercial library conversion interface
picks.reason: Provides batch filtering, file-manager integration and CD-ripping tools.
picks.tradeoff: The trial is time-limited, some codec/automation options are Windows-only, and the full EULA remains a research gap.

picks.label: Scripted multimedia transformations
picks.reason: Provides explicit codec and filter commands suitable for reproducible batches.
picks.tradeoff: The command line demands precise stream and format choices; a successful command can still produce an unintended quality change.

recipes.title: Choose language annotation or acoustic measurement tools
recipes.description: Distinguish labeling what happened in a recording from measuring the acoustic signal. Many research projects need both and an explicit interchange workflow.

picks.label: Hierarchical multimodal annotation
picks.reason: Synchronizes audio/video with time-aligned tiers, controlled vocabularies and structured EAF documents.
picks.tradeoff: Playback depends on codecs and platform; tier design and annotation agreement need their own protocol.

picks.label: Phonetic signal measurements
picks.reason: Provides speech-oriented acoustic analysis and scripting alongside annotation.
picks.tradeoff: Pitch/formant parameters and segmentation choices affect measurements.

picks.label: Layered audio inspection
picks.reason: Combines spectrograms, annotation and available analysis layers for detailed review.
picks.tradeoff: It does not replace a corpus annotation scheme or a validated phonetic measurement method.

recipes.title: Choose a desktop globe or GIS workspace
recipes.description: Choose visual geographic context versus data processing. Imagery access, content rights and project formats determine long-term portability.

picks.label: Open virtual-globe exploration
picks.reason: Provides map themes and globe-based geographic exploration.
picks.tradeoff: Available map sources have different coverage and rights.

picks.label: Google imagery and KML context
picks.reason: Provides desktop imagery exploration, historical views and GIS import/export.
picks.tradeoff: Desktop downloads end on 25 June 2027; imagery attribution and bulk-download restrictions still apply.

picks.label: Data editing and spatial analysis
picks.reason: Provides a full GIS workbench for local layers and processing.
picks.tradeoff: It needs explicitly sourced datasets; it does not automatically include the same imagery service.

recipes.title: Prepare or maintain an annotated phylogenetic tree figure
recipes.description: These viewers present already inferred trees. Inspect rooting, branch units, metadata and uncertainty before making a publication figure.

picks.label: Current FigTree successor
picks.reason: Combines tree/metadata display and export with desktop packages and local browser operation.
picks.tradeoff: Temporal interpretations require valid dates and models; the viewer does not establish inference quality.

picks.label: Legacy figure compatibility
picks.reason: Can reproduce an existing FigTree-based presentation workflow.
picks.tradeoff: The upstream README says PearTree supersedes it; ongoing FigTree support is not assumed.

recipes.title: Measure motion from video and analyze the resulting data
recipes.description: Choose a calibrated physics-video workflow for trajectories, image analysis for pixel/region measurements, and a plotting tool for exported data. These stages are complementary.

picks.label: Calibrated trajectory and model comparison
picks.reason: Tracks objects, overlays vectors and compares particle models against recorded motion.
picks.tradeoff: Perspective, frame timing and calibration errors propagate into velocity and acceleration; test the actual video format.

picks.label: Image and region analysis
picks.reason: Provides a plugin-based scientific image-analysis environment for supported image sequences.
picks.tradeoff: A suitable method/plugin and calibration are needed; not every image workflow is a physics trajectory measurement.

picks.label: Inspect and fit exported measurements
picks.reason: Combines data import, plotting and fitting after acquisition.
picks.tradeoff: The plotting stage cannot recover missing calibration or correct an invalid tracking model.
